stage: MQTT Client durable outgoing PUBLISH and ACK transitions
behavior: Private numeric TCP Client accepts QoS0, QoS1 and QoS2 through the existing PublishAsync admission. QoS0 uses volatile native output.
QoS1/2 snapshot and attempt are atomic before any PUBLISH output. First output uses DUP clear.
Known prior attempt authorizes same-session duplicate PUBLISH and an early ACK. Unattempted recovered snapshot commits OUT_ATTEMPT before its first output.
Positive PUBREC commits before PUBREL. Duplicate positive PUBREC can repeat PUBREL without another commit. PUBACK, negative PUBREC and PUBCOMP commit before local completion/identifier reuse.
Requests pin the actual native attempt/ACK duty. A late Close or timeout keeps physical effects and peer facts. Uncertain storage withholds local success and requires recovery.
Recovery checks canonical wire, MQTT id and phase against the Writer snapshot. No old application Future is fabricated.
fixture: Literal TCP peer sees exact PUBLISH and PUBREL bytes and committed model sequence at peer reception.
Actual held final sync during first attempt or ACK with no premature wire/Future output, original timeout and Close.
Real native files, explicit close/reopen and same-session recovery, preserved id and DUP, PUBREL-only replay, coalesced early PUBACK, and pre-existing unattempted records.
Negative PUBREC in MQTT5, metadata quota refusal, pre-IO first write refusal, failed publication sync with written witness, identifier reuse, and QoS0 no-store.
Concurrent application Inbox ACK plus live receive retained from preceding stage.

real_broker_smoke.scope: Continuously running numeric loopback broker, completed QoS1/2 in two generations per protocol per platform. Independent literal subscriber. Native Windows Client reaches WSL through localhost forwarding. No broker ACK cuts, broker restart or native Linux performance.

retained_failure.reason: Initial probe used a recovery wall time older than the second connection end record. Recovery correctly refused. The fixture advanced its trusted clock.

boundaries: Durable factory is private. Subscribe/unsubscribe intents and durable graceful disconnect are not yet integrated.
Each outgoing checkpoint is a native commit. No group-commit, throughput or tail-latency acceptance from these pass/fail checks.
NOT_SENT still describes bytes accepted by the original connection. A recorded attempt may be pending for later session resumption.
Remaining transport/authentication adapters, coordinated storage/transport fencing, crash/compaction and native 72-hour production qualification remain open.
